question: Identify the scion and rootstock in a grafted plant.

draft.raw: O1|P1.1,P1.2,P1.6|Subject: Grafting|material time or condition, or none|The scion is the upper part of the combined plant, typically joined to the rootstock at the soil line, and the rootstock is the lower part, which provides the roots. references.label: P1.1
references.text: Grafting or graftage[1] is a horticultural technique whereby tissues of plants are joined so as to continue their growth together.

references.label: P1.2
references.text: The upper part of the combined plant is called the scion (/ˈsaɪən/) while the lower part is called the rootstock.

references.label: P1.6
references.text: The scion is typically joined to the rootstock at the soil line; however, top-work grafting may occur far above this line, leaving an understock consisting of the lower part of the trunk and the root system.
